body.statement: For fixed \(q\), when \(\widehat\psi\) and \(\widehat\Sigma_C\) use the corrected coherent projector in Theorem 8, \(\sqrt n(C\widehat\psi-C\psi)\rightsquigarrow N(0,\Sigma_C)\), \(\widehat\Sigma_C\to_P\Sigma_C\), and the Gaussian maximum-\(t\) critical value computed from the correlation matrix of \(\widehat\Sigma_C\) gives simultaneous coverage converging to \(1-\alpha\) for all \(q\) coordinates of \(\theta=C\psi\).
body.justification: The application compares several adjacent smoking levels, so scalar pointwise intervals do not answer the scientific question.
body.gap: The closest hidden-treatment theory is centered on a binary contrast and does not provide fixed-dimensional joint maximum-\(t\) inference for ordered multilevel effects.
body.consumer: It supports one familywise-valid assessment of all declared six-bin maternal-smoking contrasts.
body.proof_tex:
Multiplying the expansion in Theorem 8 by the fixed matrix \(C\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n(C\widehat\psi-C\psi)
 &=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nC\phi^{\mathrm{eff}}(O_i)+o_P(1)\\
 &\rightsquigarrow N(0,CV_{\mathrm{eff}}C^{\mathsf T})
 =N(0,\Sigma_C). \tag{65}
\end{aligned}
\]
Consistency of \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\) and continuity of finite matrix multiplication give \(\widehat\Sigma_C\to_P\Sigma_C\).  Positive definiteness of \(\Sigma_C\) makes every diagonal entry positive, so standardization is continuous and the estimated correlation matrix \(\widehat R_C\) converges in probability to the correlation matrix \(R_C\).

For fixed \(q\), a Gaussian vector with positive-definite covariance has a continuous positive density.  Hence the boundary of each rectangle \([-t,t]^q\) has probability zero, and each nonempty shell between two such rectangles has positive probability.  Thus the distribution function of \(\max_{r\leq q}|Z_r|\), for \(Z\sim N(0,R_C)\), is continuous and strictly increasing between zero and one.  If deterministic correlation matrices \(R_m\to R_C\), their Gaussian densities converge pointwise and are dominated on compact sets; Gaussian tail bounds make the omitted complement uniformly negligible.  Therefore their rectangle probabilities converge, and the corresponding \((1-\alpha)\)-quantiles converge.  Applying this deterministic statement on every almost-surely convergent subsequence of \(\widehat R_C\) proves convergence in probability of the estimated Gaussian maximum-\(t\) critical value.  Combining that quantile convergence with (65) and consistent coordinate standard errors yields
\[
 P\!\left(
 |\sqrt n(C\widehat\psi-C\psi)_r|\leq
 \widehat c_{1-\alpha}\sqrt{\widehat\Sigma_{C,rr}}
 \text{ for all }r\leq q\right)\longrightarrow1-\alpha. \tag{66}
\]
The condition \(C\mathbf 1_K=0\) makes each row a treatment contrast; full row rank and positive information exclude redundant or zero-variance reported coordinates.
